hook: SCP-1422 is a short, dry report about a gap in the Foundation's own knowledge that went unnoticed for a very long time. The anomaly concerns a famous real-world national park, and part of the fun is how completely ordinary that place is. Read the evidence list carefully, since the joke and the chill come from the same details.
whyItMatters: It is an anomaly defined entirely by absence: no object, no entity, only a hole in what an entire organization knows. The file turns that into a worry about whether the Foundation can ever see its own blind spots, since by definition nobody inside would notice. Its Neutralized classification, and the doubts attached to it, keep it unsettling long after the last line.
thingsToNotice:
The blind spot is Yellowstone, and the proof reads like a social survey: zero of five thousand staff had heard of it, including Wyoming residents and three people embedded in the Parks Service, no staff purchases, no searches for Old Faithful, and interviewees recalling conversations where the park should have come up but never did. It was found by accident, when Junior Researcher Scranton wrote up a family trip to Yellowstone that he had lived through inside another anomaly's alternate reality, and Dr. Graff realised the place was real and world-famous.

The hypotheses get worse as they go: maybe the park did not exist until Scranton came back and reality rewrote itself around it, maybe every memory of it was being erased as it formed, maybe someone wanted activity there hidden from the Foundation and could hide themselves too. Graff's closing note admits the effect may simply have moved to other places, people or concepts, which would make it Keter-ubique, and leaves the reader wondering what they themselves cannot see.

related.note: Named in one hypothesis as research that might someday counter effects like this one.
